detailed_rationale:
TBO Tek's headline Q4 FY26 revenue growth of 83% YoY (to Rs 814cr) is a much bigger number than the platform's actual transaction growth: Gross Transaction Value (GTV), the truer measure of underlying B2B travel-distribution activity, grew just 29% YoY to Rs 10,079cr, and full-year GTV grew only 19% to Rs 36,809cr. More tellingly, consolidated net profit rose only 2% YoY (to Rs 60.1cr) despite that 83% revenue surge - gross profit was up 59% and adjusted EBITDA up 40%, so a large chunk of the incremental revenue is not converting to bottom-line growth at all. This is a real growth-quality gap, not a rounding difference, and the quant model's growth_divergence_flag is correctly triggered.

The underlying business does have genuine strengths: it is a B2B travel distribution platform connecting suppliers to travel agents/OTAs globally, with the Hotels & Ancillaries segment (Europe +22%, APAC +46%, MEA +22% FY26) doing the heavy lifting, and management characterized FY26 as a 'real-world stress test' that the platform came through with India showing a second-half recovery. ROE (28.9%) and ROCE (29.2%) are strong, and quality_score of 88 reflects a genuinely well-run business model with real network effects.

Reverse-DCF read: at 64.6x earnings, the market is pricing in a continuation of GTV growth well above the 19-29% actually being delivered, essentially assuming the revenue-to-GTV gap either continues (unlikely to be sustainable without margin dilution) or profit growth catches up sharply. That's a rich multiple for a business whose most recent quarter showed profit growing at just 2% - the valuation leaves very little room for a miss.
recommendation_rationale: Quant composite lands on Hold (61.6/60.5) already reflecting the quality/growth-divergence tension - strong fundamentals (ROE/ROCE ~29%) but a rich multiple (value_score just 25.9) and a flagged growth divergence. My own read of GTV vs. revenue vs. profit confirms the divergence is real and material, reinforcing Hold rather than suggesting either a rescue or an escalation.
summary: TBO Tek is a genuinely strong B2B travel-distribution platform, but its headline 83% revenue growth this quarter significantly overstates the underlying business: the more meaningful transaction-volume metric (GTV) grew a much more modest 29%, and profit grew just 2% year-on-year despite the revenue surge. Management called FY26 a stress test the platform passed, and growth in international hotel bookings (Europe, Asia-Pacific, Middle East) is real, but at roughly 65x earnings the stock is priced for far more consistent profit growth than it has just delivered - we'd want to see profit catch up to the revenue optics before getting more constructive.
positive_para: Genuine network-effect B2B travel platform with strong capital efficiency (ROE 28.9%, ROCE 29.2%); international hotel/ancillary segment growing at healthy double-digit rates across Europe, APAC and MEA; management navigated a genuinely difficult FY26 (multiple disruptions cited) without losing GTV growth; India business showing second-half recovery.
negative_para: The 83% revenue growth headline is not matched by GTV (+29%) or profit (+2%) growth in the same quarter - a real earnings-quality gap that suggests margin dilution or a change in revenue mix/recognition rather than pure organic scaling; at 64.6x PE the valuation assumes this gap resolves favorably, which is not guaranteed; travel-distribution platforms remain exposed to macro/geopolitical disruption to travel demand, as FY26 itself demonstrated.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~64.6x earnings against GTV growth of only 19-29% and quarterly profit growth of just 2%, the multiple is pricing a re-acceleration of profit growth toward the historical (36% 3yr revenue CAGR) pace that the most recent quarter did not deliver. This is rich, not fair, given the current profit-growth reality; we'd size any position with the recognition that a lot of good news is already in the price.
